paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus sees what's real, and a good reputation isn't the same as a living faith. Sardis had a name for being alive, yet Jesus says, "you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead" (Revelation 3:1). I think that stings, because it's the church that looked great on the outside. So He says, "Wake up and strengthen what remains" (Revelation 3:2), and He doesn't say it to shame them, He says it because there's still something left to save.

Now look at Philadelphia, friend, because Jesus sees them just as clearly. They had only a little strength, yet they kept His word and did not deny His name (Revelation 3:8). That's what He notices, not how big or loud they were. He holds the key of David, so the door He opens, no one can shut (Revelation 3:7). He tells them, "I am coming soon. Hold fast to what you have" (Revelation 3:11), and that is why my ovens stay ready, friend, not because I know when, but because He's coming.

So what do you do with that today, baker? You stay awake, you hold on, and you let Jesus be the One who says what you're worth. To the one who overcomes, He promises white garments, a name that is never blotted out of the Book of Life, and a place in the temple of His God that he will never leave (Revelation 3:5, 3:12). Nobody can shut a door He opened (Revelation 3:8), and He tells Philadelphia to hold fast so no one will take their crown (Revelation 3:11). And this message isn't finished yet, friend, so keep your ears open.
